title: Royal Crest Literature in English: Mpho's Search by Sandra Braude (reader's guide)
_note: Plot facts only from the publisher's description (Oxford University Press Southern Africa). say = sent to ElevenLabs; cap = on-screen caption.

lines.say: A farm in South Africa. A sheep goes missing.
lines.cap: A farm in South Africa. A sheep goes missing.

lines.say: And a boy must leave the only home he knows.
lines.cap: And a boy must leave the only home he knows.

lines.say: This is Mpho's Search, a novel by Sandra Braude. Let's read it like Literature students.
lines.cap: This is Mpho’s Search, a novel by Sandra Braude. Let’s read it like Literature students.

lines.say: The story moves between two settings. Baas du Toit's farm in the countryside, and the busy streets of Johannesburg.
lines.cap: The story moves between two settings: Baas du Toit’s farm in the countryside, and the busy streets of Johannesburg.

lines.say: Notice the word Baas. It's Afrikaans for boss, or master.
lines.cap: Notice the word “Baas”. It’s Afrikaans for boss, or master.

lines.say: When the farm owner is called Baas, the writer shows us who holds the power.
lines.cap: When the farm owner is called “Baas”, the writer shows us who holds the power.

lines.say: After a sheep goes missing, Mpho is forced off the farm.
lines.cap: After a sheep goes missing, Mpho is forced off the farm.

lines.say: So he sets out for Johannesburg, to find his father.
lines.cap: So he sets out for Johannesburg, to find his father.

lines.say: In the city, life on the streets is hard. But Mpho makes a friend, Themba.
lines.cap: In the city, life on the streets is hard. But Mpho makes a friend: Themba.

lines.say: Together they earn a living with a shoe-shine business.
lines.cap: Together they earn a living with a shoe-shine business.

lines.say: That small business tells us a lot about Mpho. He is determined, hard-working and full of hope.
lines.cap: That small business tells us a lot about Mpho: determined, hard-working and full of hope.

lines.say: And his search carries us all the way to South Africa's first democratic elections, in nineteen ninety-four.
lines.cap: And his search carries us all the way to South Africa’s first democratic elections, in 1994.

lines.say: So this is not only one boy's story. It is the story of a country changing.
lines.cap: So this is not only one boy’s story. It is the story of a country changing.

lines.say: Here are five big themes to track as you read.
lines.cap: Five big themes to track as you read.

lines.say: Family and belonging. Survival. Friendship. Power and injustice. And hope, and freedom.
lines.cap: Family and belonging. Survival. Friendship. Power and injustice. Hope and freedom.

lines.say: Three characters to know. Mpho, the searcher. Themba, his friend in the city. And Baas du Toit, the farm owner whose power changes Mpho's life.
lines.cap: Three characters: Mpho, the searcher. Themba, his friend in the city. Baas du Toit, the farm owner whose power changes Mpho’s life.

lines.say: As you read, keep notes. Highlight the key moments, and write in the margin what each one shows.
lines.cap: As you read, keep notes. Highlight the key moments, and write in the margin what each one shows.

lines.say: Ready for a class discussion? Try these.
lines.cap: Ready for a class discussion? Try these.

lines.say: Why does Mpho leave the farm? And how does the setting change, from the farm to the city?
lines.cap: Why does Mpho leave the farm? How does the setting change, from the farm to the city?

lines.say: What does Themba's friendship give Mpho? And why do the elections matter in the story?
lines.cap: What does Themba’s friendship give Mpho? Why do the elections matter in the story?

lines.say: For me, Mpho shows that being far from home is not the end of hope.
lines.cap: For me, Mpho shows that being far from home is not the end of hope.

lines.say: Royal Crest Academy, Bikita. Literature in English, on the Cambridge syllabus.
lines.cap: Royal Crest Academy, Bikita. Literature in English, on the Cambridge syllabus.
